_comment: Editorial plan for the launch library. Slugs are fixed so pieces can link to each other. 'brief' lists the scope and anchor facts to verify before writing; it is direction, not copy.

articles.title: How Much Protein Do You Actually Need?
articles.brief: RDA 0.8 g/kg vs. evidence for higher intakes when training (~1.6 g/kg, Morton 2018) and for older adults (1.0-1.2 g/kg, PROT-AGE). Per-meal distribution, plant vs animal sources, protein quality, a food table, kidney-safety evidence in healthy people, who should be cautious.

articles.title: Fiber: The Most Underrated Nutrient on Your Plate
articles.brief: Soluble vs insoluble vs fermentable; WHO 2023 guidance (at least 25 g/day), 14 g per 1,000 kcal; Reynolds 2019 Lancet meta-analysis; most people fall short; how to increase without bloating; food table; supplements such as psyllium.

articles.title: Carbs, Explained: Sugar, Starch and Whole Grains
articles.brief: Types of carbohydrate, glycemic index and load and their limits, whole vs refined grains, WHO free-sugars limits (<10% and ideally <5% of energy), AHA added sugar limits, low-carb diets evidence in brief, carbs for training.

articles.title: Fats, Decoded: Saturated, Unsaturated, Trans and Omega-3
articles.brief: Fat types and food sources, saturated fat guidance (WHO <10% energy; AHA <6%), trans fat elimination (WHO REPLACE, <1% energy), omega-3 EPA/DHA and fish twice a week, seed-oil claims vs evidence, cooking oils.

articles.title: The Mediterranean Diet: What It Is and Why It Keeps Winning
articles.brief: What the pattern includes, PREDIMED trial (about 30% lower major cardiovascular events; 2018 republication), other evidence (diabetes, cognition), how to adapt it to non-Mediterranean cuisines, a sample day, cost-saving swaps.

articles.title: How Much Water Do You Really Need?
articles.brief: Origin of the 8-glasses rule, National Academies adequate intakes (about 3.7 L men, 2.7 L women total water from all drinks and food), EFSA values, thirst and urine colour, needs in heat, exercise, pregnancy; hyponatremia from overdrinking; do coffee and tea count. Link to /tools/water.

articles.title: Vitamins and Supplements: Who Actually Needs Them?
articles.brief: USPSTF 2022: insufficient evidence for multivitamins to prevent CVD or cancer, recommends against beta-carotene and vitamin E. Who benefits: folic acid before and during early pregnancy, B12 for vegans and older adults, vitamin D in deficiency or low sun, iron in deficiency, iodine. Upper limits and risks, third-party testing, drug interactions.

articles.title: Ultra-Processed Foods: What They Are and Why They Matter
articles.brief: NOVA classification and its criticisms, Hall 2019 NIH inpatient trial (about 500 kcal/day more on the ultra-processed diet), BMJ 2024 umbrella review (Lane et al.), how to spot UPFs on labels, realistic swaps, not all UPFs are equal.

articles.title: How to Read a Nutrition Label in 30 Seconds
articles.brief: Serving size traps, % Daily Value and the 5%/20% rule (FDA), added sugars line, sodium, fibre and protein, ingredient order, health-claim wording, front-of-pack systems (traffic lights, Nutri-Score), per-100 g comparisons.

articles.title: How Much Exercise Do You Need? The Guidelines, Made Practical
articles.brief: WHO 2020 guidelines: adults 150-300 min moderate or 75-150 min vigorous per week plus muscle strengthening on 2+ days; older adults add balance work on 3 days; children 60 min/day. Talk test, any movement counts, what a real week looks like, benefits with size of effect.

articles.title: Strength Training for Beginners: A Simple Full-Body Plan
articles.brief: Why lift (mortality, bone, metabolic health; Momma 2022 meta-analysis found 10-17% lower mortality with 30-60 min/week), movement patterns (squat, hinge, push, pull, carry), a 2-3 day full-body plan with sets and reps, how to choose weights (reps in reserve), warm-up, form priorities, home options. Link to /exercises.

articles.title: Zone 2 and VO2 Max: The Cardio That Buys You Years
articles.brief: What VO2 max is and why cardiorespiratory fitness predicts mortality (Mandsager 2018 JAMA Network Open; Kokkinos 2022), what zone 2 means (talk test, roughly 60-70% max heart rate), honest evidence on zone 2 vs higher intensity, weekly template mixing easy volume with intervals (e.g. 4x4), how wearables estimate VO2 max. Link to /tools/heart-rate-zones.

articles.title: Progressive Overload: The One Rule Behind Getting Stronger
articles.brief: The principle, ways to progress (load, reps, sets, range, tempo, density), double progression example, proximity to failure, volume per muscle group per week (Schoenfeld dose-response), plateaus and deloads, tracking.

articles.title: How Many Steps a Day Do You Really Need?
articles.brief: Origin of 10,000 (1960s Japanese pedometer marketing), Paluch 2022 Lancet Public Health meta-analysis (benefit plateaus about 6,000-8,000 for 60+, 8,000-10,000 under 60), Lee 2019 JAMA Internal Medicine in older women, Banach 2023, cadence and intensity, practical ways to add steps.

articles.title: Stretching and Mobility: What Helps and What Is Hype
articles.brief: Static vs dynamic stretching, what stretching does and does not do (does not meaningfully prevent soreness per Cochrane; limited injury-prevention evidence), strength through full range improves flexibility, warm-up guidance, a 10-minute routine, when tightness needs assessment.

articles.title: Rest Days Are Training Days: Recovery, Explained
articles.brief: Supercompensation, sleep as the main recovery tool, protein and energy intake, active recovery, DOMS, overreaching vs overtraining syndrome, RED-S (relative energy deficiency in sport, IOC 2023 consensus), evidence check on ice baths, massage guns and foam rolling, how to schedule rest.

articles.title: Creatine: What the Evidence Actually Says
articles.brief: How creatine works, ISSN 2017 position stand, 3-5 g/day of creatine monohydrate, loading is optional, effects on strength and lean mass, water weight, safety and kidney myths in healthy people, emerging and still uncertain evidence on cognition and older adults, who should check with a doctor.

articles.title: HIIT vs. Steady-State Cardio: Which Is Better?
articles.brief: Definitions, time efficiency, comparable fitness and fat-loss outcomes when work is matched (Wewege 2017; Viana 2019), injury and adherence considerations, example sessions, who should start gentler, combining both in a week.

articles.title: How Much Sleep Do You Need? A Guide by Age
articles.brief: AASM/SRS consensus (7 or more hours for adults), National Sleep Foundation ranges by age including children and teens, sleep quality vs quantity, effects of short sleep, can you catch up at weekends, short sleepers are rare, signs you are not getting enough. Link to /tools/sleep-cycles.

articles.title: Sleep Hygiene: 12 Habits That Actually Help
articles.brief: Consistent wake time, morning light, caffeine cut-off, alcohol, cool dark quiet bedroom (roughly 16-19 C / 60-67 F is commonly advised), wind-down routine, screens and light at night, exercise timing, late heavy meals, bed only for sleep, getting up when you cannot sleep, managing worry. Be honest that hygiene alone does not cure chronic insomnia.

articles.title: Insomnia: Why You Can't Sleep and What Actually Works
articles.brief: Acute vs chronic insomnia (at least 3 nights a week for 3 months), the 3P model, CBT-I as first-line treatment (ACP 2016, AASM 2021) with its components (stimulus control, sleep restriction, cognitive work), digital CBT-I, medications and their limits including orexin antagonists, melatonin evidence, when to see a doctor.

articles.title: Your Body Clock: Circadian Rhythm, Light and Timing
articles.brief: The suprachiasmatic nucleus, light as the main time cue, melatonin timing, chronotypes, social jet lag, morning light and dim evenings, shift work and health, jet lag strategies, teenagers' delayed clocks.

articles.title: Caffeine, Alcohol and Your Sleep
articles.brief: Adenosine and caffeine half-life (about 5 hours on average with wide variation), Drake 2013 (caffeine 6 hours before bed reduced sleep by more than an hour), 400 mg/day upper guidance for most adults, alcohol as a sedative that fragments sleep and suppresses REM, practical cut-offs, nicotine.

articles.title: How to Nap Without Wrecking Your Night
articles.brief: Sleep pressure and the afternoon dip, 10-20 minute power naps vs a full 90-minute cycle, sleep inertia, nap before about 3 pm, the coffee nap, NASA pilot nap study (26 minutes; alertness and performance gains), who should avoid naps (insomnia), long daytime naps as a possible marker of health problems.

articles.title: Snoring and Sleep Apnea: Signs You Shouldn't Ignore
articles.brief: Simple snoring vs obstructive sleep apnea, symptoms and risk factors, STOP-Bang screening, estimated 936 million adults affected worldwide (Benjafield 2019), health risks, sleep studies including home tests, CPAP, oral appliances, weight loss, tirzepatide approval for OSA with obesity (FDA, December 2024), positional therapy.

articles.title: Stress: What It Does to Your Body and How to Dial It Down
articles.brief: Acute stress response (sympathetic system, HPA axis, cortisol), when stress helps, chronic stress and health, physical signs, evidence-based tools: physical activity, sleep, slow breathing, social support, time in nature, CBT techniques, mindfulness; when stress becomes a disorder.

articles.title: Anxiety: What It Is, What It Isn't and What Helps
articles.brief: Normal anxiety vs anxiety disorders, WHO figure of about 301 million people living with an anxiety disorder (2019), types (GAD, panic, social, phobias), physical symptoms, CBT and exposure, SSRIs and SNRIs, self-help (exercise, caffeine, sleep, breathing), when and how to get help. Include crisis guidance.

articles.title: Depression: Signs, Causes and Treatments That Work
articles.brief: Sadness vs depression, core symptoms and the two-week criterion, WHO estimate of about 280 million people, causes as a mix of biology, psychology and circumstances, treatments (psychotherapies such as CBT and behavioural activation, antidepressants, combined treatment, exercise as an adjunct), how to support someone, when it is an emergency. Include crisis guidance; non-stigmatising language.

articles.title: Burnout: How to Recognize It and Actually Recover
articles.brief: ICD-11 definition as an occupational phenomenon with three dimensions (exhaustion, mental distance or cynicism, reduced efficacy), burnout vs depression, the six areas of work-life mismatch (Maslach and Leiter), individual steps and why workplace causes matter, recovery timeline, when to see a professional.

articles.title: Meditation and Mindfulness: What the Science Says
articles.brief: What mindfulness is, Goyal 2014 JAMA Internal Medicine meta-analysis (moderate evidence for anxiety, depression and pain), Hoge 2023 JAMA Psychiatry (MBSR non-inferior to escitalopram for anxiety disorders), realistic expectations, possible adverse effects for some people, a 5-minute beginner practice, apps vs courses.

articles.title: Exercise for Mental Health: The Most Underused Treatment
articles.brief: Noetel 2024 BMJ network meta-analysis (walking or jogging, yoga and strength training effective for depression), Singh 2023 BJSM umbrella review, proposed mechanisms, what dose helps, how to start when motivation is low, exercise alongside, not instead of, professional treatment.

articles.title: Loneliness Is a Health Issue. Here's What to Do About It.
articles.brief: Loneliness vs social isolation, Holt-Lunstad 2015 meta-analysis (26-32% higher mortality risk), US Surgeon General 2023 advisory, WHO Commission on Social Connection 2025 report (about 1 in 6 people affected), mechanisms, what helps (regular contact, shared activities, volunteering, small talk), technology's mixed role.

articles.title: Blood Pressure Numbers, Explained
articles.brief: What systolic and diastolic mean, ACC/AHA categories (normal <120/80; elevated 120-129/<80; stage 1 130-139 or 80-89; stage 2 140+ or 90+; severe >180 and/or >120) and the different ESC and other international thresholds (140/90), how to measure correctly at home, white-coat and masked hypertension, lifestyle changes with expected mmHg effect, when medication is used. Link to /tools/blood-pressure.

articles.title: Cholesterol: What LDL, HDL and Triglycerides Really Mean
articles.brief: Lipoproteins, standard lipid panel and typical target ranges in mg/dL and mmol/L, why LDL and non-HDL or ApoB matter most, HDL is a marker rather than a target, Lp(a) one-time test, diet and lifestyle effects, statins (benefit, muscle symptoms and the nocebo effect), fasting vs non-fasting tests.

articles.title: Heart Attack and Stroke: Warning Signs to Act On Fast
articles.brief: Heart attack symptoms including less typical presentations in women, older adults and people with diabetes; what to do (call emergency services, aspirin only if advised and not allergic); stroke FAST / BE-FAST and time-critical treatment; TIA as a warning; cardiac arrest vs heart attack, CPR and AEDs. Emergency-first tone.

articles.title: The DASH Diet and Salt: Eating for Lower Blood Pressure
articles.brief: DASH trial results (Appel 1997: about 5.5 mmHg systolic overall, around 11 mmHg in people with hypertension), DASH-Sodium, WHO sodium limit (<2 g sodium, i.e. <5 g salt per day) and typical global intake of about 10.8 g salt, where salt hides, potassium and salt substitutes (SSaSS trial 2021, with the kidney-disease caution), a sample day.

articles.title: Resting Heart Rate and HRV: What Your Wearable Is Telling You
articles.brief: Normal resting heart rate (60-100 bpm for adults; lower in trained people), how to measure, what trends mean, heart rate variability and why to compare only against your own baseline, factors that move both (sleep, alcohol, illness, stress, training), accuracy limits of wearables, when a number needs medical attention (including irregular rhythm notifications).

articles.title: Know Your Risk: What Really Drives Heart Disease
articles.brief: Cardiovascular disease as the leading cause of death worldwide (WHO), INTERHEART (nine modifiable factors explain about 90% of first heart-attack risk), AHA Life's Essential 8, non-modifiable factors (age, family history, sex), risk calculators (PREVENT, SCORE2, QRISK3), women-specific risk enhancers, what to do with your risk.

articles.title: Omega-3 and Fish Oil: Does It Help Your Heart?
articles.brief: Eating fish vs taking supplements, mixed trial results (VITAL and STRENGTH largely neutral; REDUCE-IT positive for high-dose icosapent ethyl in people with high triglycerides), atrial fibrillation signal at higher doses, guidance to eat fish about twice a week, plant sources (ALA), who might be prescribed omega-3.

articles.title: Your Gut Microbiome, Explained Without the Hype
articles.brief: What the microbiome is (Sender 2016: roughly 38 trillion bacteria, about a 1:1 ratio with human cells), what it does (short-chain fatty acids, immune training, barrier function), what shapes it (diet diversity, fibre, antibiotics, birth and early life), what is and is not proven about links with mood and weight, why consumer microbiome tests are not clinically validated, the gut-brain axis.

articles.title: Probiotics, Prebiotics and Fermented Foods: What's Worth It?
articles.brief: Definitions, strain-specific evidence, where probiotics have support (preventing antibiotic-associated diarrhoea) and where guidelines do not recommend them (AGA 2020 for most digestive conditions), Wastyk 2021 Cell fermented-food study, prebiotic fibres and foods, safety in immunocompromised people, how to choose.

articles.title: Bloating: Common Causes and What Actually Helps
articles.brief: Bloating vs distension, common causes (constipation, swallowed air, FODMAPs, lactose, IBS, fast fibre increases, hormonal cycle), strategies with evidence (regular meals, slower eating, gentle movement, peppermint oil for IBS, targeted food trials), what does not work (detox teas), red flags needing a doctor (persistent bloating especially over 50, weight loss, bleeding; ovarian cancer awareness).

articles.title: Constipation: What Works, in Order of Evidence
articles.brief: Definition and the Bristol stool chart, fibre and psyllium, fluids, kiwifruit and prunes trials, movement, toilet posture and routine, over-the-counter options (osmotic laxatives such as polyethylene glycol; short-term stimulants), medicines that cause constipation, red flags.

articles.title: Acid Reflux and Heartburn: Causes, Fixes and When to Worry
articles.brief: What reflux and GERD are, typical and atypical symptoms, lifestyle measures with evidence (weight loss, raising the head of the bed, not eating within about 3 hours of bed, personal trigger foods, stopping smoking), antacids, H2 blockers and PPIs with sensible use, alarm features (trouble swallowing, bleeding, weight loss), chest pain needs urgent assessment.

articles.title: IBS and the Low-FODMAP Diet: A Practical Guide
articles.brief: What IBS is (Rome IV criteria, subtypes) and how it is diagnosed, the gut-brain interaction, first-line advice, low-FODMAP diet in three phases (restrict, reintroduce, personalise) ideally with a dietitian, response in roughly half to three quarters of people, other treatments (soluble fibre, peppermint oil, gut-directed psychological therapy, medication), red flags.

articles.title: Food Intolerance vs. Food Allergy: How to Tell the Difference
articles.brief: Immune allergy (IgE, anaphylaxis) vs intolerance, the most common allergens, lactose malabsorption (about two thirds of adults worldwide; Storhaug 2017), coeliac disease (about 1%; test before going gluten-free), non-coeliac gluten sensitivity, why IgG food-intolerance tests are not recommended, supervised elimination and reintroduction.

articles.title: Metabolism 101: What Actually Burns Your Calories
articles.brief: Components of daily energy expenditure (BMR about 60-70%, thermic effect of food about 10%, NEAT, exercise), Pontzer 2021 Science (metabolism stable from 20 to 60, then declining slowly), what really influences it (body size and lean mass), myths (metabolism-boosting foods, starvation mode), adaptive thermogenesis. Link to /tools/tdee.

articles.title: Weight Loss That Lasts: What the Evidence Says
articles.brief: Energy balance without oversimplifying, a 5-10% loss brings measurable health benefits, why diets work short term and regain is common, what predicts maintenance (National Weight Control Registry patterns: activity, self-monitoring, consistency), protein and resistance training to protect muscle, sleep and stress, medications and surgery as legitimate tools, weight stigma and health behaviours beyond the scale.

articles.title: Blood Sugar Basics: Glucose, HbA1c and What's Normal
articles.brief: How glucose and insulin work, diagnostic thresholds (ADA: fasting 100-125 mg/dL and HbA1c 5.7-6.4% for prediabetes; fasting 126+ mg/dL, HbA1c 6.5%+ or 2-hour OGTT 200+ for diabetes; give mmol/L too and note WHO differences), post-meal spikes in healthy people, continuous glucose monitors for people without diabetes (limited evidence), what helps (fibre, movement after meals, sleep).

articles.title: Insulin Resistance and Prediabetes: The Warning You Can Act On
articles.brief: What insulin resistance is, risk factors and signs (acanthosis nigricans, waist size), prediabetes prevalence (CDC: about 1 in 3 US adults, most unaware), the Diabetes Prevention Program (lifestyle cut progression by 58%, metformin by 31%), what to change first, remission of early type 2 diabetes (DiRECT trial).

articles.title: Thyroid 101: Signs Yours Is Running Fast or Slow
articles.brief: What the thyroid does, hypothyroidism vs hyperthyroidism symptoms, common causes (Hashimoto's, Graves' disease, iodine deficiency globally), TSH and free T4 testing, subclinical hypothyroidism, levothyroxine basics (taken on an empty stomach; biotin can interfere with tests), thyroid supplement myths, nodules, pregnancy.

articles.title: Intermittent Fasting: An Evidence Check
articles.brief: Types (time-restricted eating, 5:2, alternate-day), randomised trials showing weight loss similar to ordinary calorie restriction (Liu 2022 NEJM; Lowe 2020 JAMA Internal Medicine), possible downsides including lean-mass loss, who should avoid it (pregnancy, history of eating disorders, some people with diabetes on glucose-lowering drugs), practical tips if you try it.

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Explained: Semaglutide, Tirzepatide and What Comes Next
articles.brief: How GLP-1 and GIP agonists work, trial results (STEP 1: about 15% average weight loss with semaglutide 2.4 mg at 68 weeks; SURMOUNT-1: up to about 21% with tirzepatide at 72 weeks; SELECT: 20% fewer major cardiovascular events), side effects and warnings, regain after stopping (STEP 1 extension), protecting muscle, who qualifies, risks of compounded or counterfeit products, oral options. Not medical advice; prescription only.

articles.title: BMI, Waist Size and Body Fat: Which Number Matters?
articles.brief: What BMI is and its WHO categories, limits (muscle, age, ethnicity; lower cut-offs for Asian populations per the WHO expert consultation), waist circumference and waist-to-height ratio (keep waist under half your height; NICE 2022), 2025 Lancet Commission on clinical obesity, body-fat measurement methods and accuracy. Link to /tools/bmi, /tools/waist-to-height and /tools/body-fat.

articles.title: The Menstrual Cycle, Phase by Phase
articles.brief: The four phases and their hormones, what is typical (cycles roughly 21-35 days in adults, bleeding up to about 7 days), ovulation signs, the cycle as a vital sign (ACOG), cycle-syncing claims vs evidence for training, tracking apps and privacy, when irregular cycles need assessment.

articles.title: Period Pain and Heavy Periods: What's Normal and What's Not
articles.brief: Primary vs secondary dysmenorrhoea, NSAIDs and heat with evidence, hormonal options, how heavy menstrual bleeding is defined (interferes with life; flooding, clots, changing protection hourly), iron deficiency, possible causes (fibroids, endometriosis, adenomyosis, bleeding disorders), endometriosis affects roughly 10% and diagnosis is often delayed for years, when to see a doctor.

articles.title: PCOS, Explained: Symptoms, Diagnosis and Management
articles.brief: What PCOS is, prevalence (WHO: 6-13% of reproductive-age women, with up to 70% undiagnosed), Rotterdam criteria and the 2023 international guideline, insulin resistance, symptoms, long-term risks, management (lifestyle, combined pill, metformin, anti-androgens, inositol evidence, fertility treatment such as letrozole), mental health, myths.

articles.title: Pregnancy Basics: Nutrition, Exercise and What to Avoid
articles.brief: Folic acid 400 mcg daily before conception and through early pregnancy, iron, iodine, vitamin D, choline and DHA; foods to avoid (listeria and toxoplasma risks, high-mercury fish, alcohol), caffeine under 200 mg/day, appropriate weight gain ranges (Institute of Medicine), exercise 150 min/week of moderate activity (ACOG) and warning signs to stop, vaccines in pregnancy, urgent symptoms. Link to /tools/due-date.

articles.title: Perimenopause and Menopause: Symptoms and Your Options
articles.brief: Definitions and timing (average age about 51; perimenopause can last several years), symptoms beyond hot flushes, hormone therapy as the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms with benefits and risks and the timing hypothesis (Menopause Society 2022 position statement), non-hormonal options (fezolinetant, some SSRIs/SNRIs, CBT), vaginal oestrogen, bone and heart health afterwards, supplement evidence.

articles.title: Your Pelvic Floor: A User's Guide
articles.brief: What the pelvic floor does, signs of weakness and of overactivity, how common urinary incontinence is, how to do pelvic floor muscle training correctly (Cochrane evidence as first-line treatment for stress incontinence), common mistakes, pregnancy and postpartum, when to see a pelvic health physiotherapist, prolapse basics.

articles.title: Breast and Cervical Screening: What to Get and When
articles.brief: Mammography recommendations (USPSTF 2024: every two years from 40 to 74; note other countries start at 50), dense breasts, breast awareness, cervical screening (Pap and HPV testing schedules, self-collection options), HPV vaccination and the WHO 90-70-90 elimination targets, what an abnormal result means, symptoms that should not wait for screening.

articles.title: Testosterone: What's Normal, What's Low and What TRT Can Do
articles.brief: What testosterone does, decline with age, diagnosing hypogonadism (symptoms plus two low morning tests; AUA uses under 300 ng/dL), causes of low levels (obesity, sleep apnea, medicines), lifestyle effects, TRT benefits and risks (TRAVERSE 2023: no excess major cardiac events but more atrial fibrillation and pulmonary embolism; fertility suppression; raised haematocrit), booster supplements lack evidence.

articles.title: Prostate Health: BPH, PSA Tests and What to Watch For
articles.brief: What the prostate does, benign prostatic hyperplasia symptoms and how common it becomes with age, treatments (lifestyle, alpha blockers, 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, procedures), prostatitis in brief, prostate cancer risk factors, PSA screening as a shared decision (USPSTF: ages 55-69), MRI before biopsy, active surveillance for low-risk disease.

articles.title: Erectile Dysfunction: Causes, the Heart Link and What Works
articles.brief: How common ED is (Massachusetts Male Aging Study), vascular, hormonal, neurological, medication-related and psychological causes, ED as an early warning sign of cardiovascular disease, lifestyle changes with evidence, PDE5 inhibitors (how they work, the nitrate interaction), other treatments, counterfeit pills, mental health and relationships.

articles.title: Male Pattern Hair Loss: What Actually Works
articles.brief: Androgenetic alopecia mechanism (DHT, genetics), how common it is, evidence-based treatments (topical and low-dose oral minoxidil, finasteride with its side-effect discussion, dutasteride off-label), weaker options (low-level light, microneedling, PRP), hair transplants, what does not work (biotin unless deficient), when shedding suggests another cause.

articles.title: Men's Mental Health: Why It Goes Unspoken and How to Start
articles.brief: Men die by suicide at more than twice the rate of women globally (WHO) yet are less often diagnosed with depression, how distress can present in men (irritability, risk-taking, alcohol, overwork), barriers to seeking help, what works (action-oriented therapy, peer groups, exercise), how to check in on a friend, crisis guidance.

articles.title: Male Fertility: The Basics Nobody Told You
articles.brief: A male factor contributes in roughly half of couples with infertility, semen analysis and WHO 2021 reference values, sperm production takes about three months, what affects sperm (heat, smoking, alcohol, obesity, anabolic steroids and testosterone therapy, varicocele, age), the sperm-count decline debate (Levine 2022 and its critics), supplements evidence, when to get tested.

articles.title: The Checkups Men Skip, Decade by Decade
articles.brief: Men visit doctors less often; by decade from the 20s to 60s+: blood pressure, lipids, diabetes screening, testicular awareness, sexual health tests, skin checks, colorectal screening from 45, the prostate conversation, abdominal aortic aneurysm ultrasound at 65-75 for men who have smoked (USPSTF), vaccines, dental and eye checks, mental health.

articles.title: Sunscreen: The Only Anti-Aging Product With Real Proof
articles.brief: UVA vs UVB, what SPF means (SPF 30 filters about 97% of UVB, SPF 50 about 98%), broad spectrum, how much to apply (2 mg per square cm; roughly a shot glass for the body) and reapplying every two hours, mineral vs chemical filters and safety, Nambour trial (regular use reduced melanoma and skin ageing), darker skin tones, vitamin D, children, shade and clothing.

articles.title: A Simple Skincare Routine That Actually Works
articles.brief: The three essentials (gentle cleanser, moisturiser, sunscreen), actives with good evidence (retinoids, vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid, AHAs and BHAs), how to introduce retinoids, routines by skin type, what is mostly marketing, patch testing, pregnancy cautions, when to see a dermatologist.

articles.title: Acne: What Causes It and What Clears It
articles.brief: Four factors in acne, over-the-counter options (benzoyl peroxide, adapalene, salicylic acid), prescription options (topical and oral antibiotics used short term with benzoyl peroxide, hormonal therapy, isotretinoin with monitoring) per AAD 2024 guidelines, diet evidence (glycaemic load, dairy), not picking, scarring, adult acne, expect 6-12 weeks for results.

articles.title: Hair Shedding and Thinning: Why It Happens and What Helps
articles.brief: Hair growth cycle and normal shedding (about 50-100 hairs a day), telogen effluvium triggers (illness, childbirth, stress, rapid weight loss, iron deficiency, thyroid disease), female pattern hair loss, alopecia areata (JAK inhibitors approved for severe cases), traction alopecia, useful blood tests, treatments, supplement evidence, timeline for regrowth.

articles.title: Oral Health: The Two-Minute Habit With Whole-Body Payoff
articles.brief: WHO: oral diseases affect about 3.5 billion people; brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, spit rather than rinse, clean between teeth, electric vs manual brushes (Cochrane), sugar frequency, gum disease stages and links with diabetes and heart disease (association, not proven causation), dental visits, mouthwash, whitening safety.

articles.title: Skin Cancer and Mole Checks: The ABCDE Guide
articles.brief: Types of skin cancer (basal cell, squamous cell, melanoma), risk factors, the ABCDE rule and the ugly duckling sign, how to do a monthly self-check, acral melanoma on palms, soles and under nails in darker skin, what a dermatologist check involves, sunbeds (IARC group 1 carcinogen), prevention.

articles.title: Collagen, Biotin and Beauty Supplements: An Evidence Check
articles.brief: Collagen peptide trials (meta-analyses suggest modest gains in skin hydration and elasticity, with industry-funding concerns), biotin (little evidence unless deficient; FDA warning that it interferes with lab tests including troponin), hair-skin-nail blends, vitamin C and zinc in deficiency, what works better (sunscreen, retinoids, not smoking, sleep).

articles.title: The Habits That Actually Predict a Longer Life
articles.brief: Li 2018 Circulation (five low-risk habits linked with about 14 more years of life expectancy at 50 for women and 12 for men), the big levers: not smoking, physical activity, diet quality, healthy weight, limited alcohol, plus sleep and social connection; genes account for a modest share of lifespan variation (about 25% in twin studies); healthspan vs lifespan; it is never too late.

articles.title: Muscle Is Your Retirement Fund: Strength and Aging
articles.brief: Sarcopenia (muscle mass falls roughly 3-8% per decade after 30, faster after 60), grip strength as a predictor (Leong 2015 Lancet PURE study), falls and independence, resistance training works at any age (Fiatarone 1990 study of nonagenarians), protein needs for older adults, power training, how to start safely.

articles.title: Healthspan: The Biomarkers Actually Worth Tracking
articles.brief: Markers with strong evidence: blood pressure, LDL or ApoB, HbA1c or fasting glucose, waist-to-height ratio, cardiorespiratory fitness, grip strength and chair-stand, kidney function, plus honest caveats on full-body MRI, epigenetic age tests and other consumer panels (false positives, overdiagnosis). How often to check and what to do with results.

articles.title: Dementia Prevention: The 14 Risk Factors You Can Change
articles.brief: Lancet Commission 2024: 14 modifiable risk factors across life that together account for about 45% of dementia cases (less education, hearing loss, high LDL cholesterol, depression, traumatic brain injury, physical inactivity, diabetes, smoking, hypertension, obesity, excessive alcohol, social isolation, air pollution, untreated vision loss); hearing aids and the ACHIEVE trial; SPRINT MIND and blood pressure; what does not work (most supplements, brain-training hype).

articles.title: Longevity Supplements and Drugs: An Evidence Check
articles.brief: NAD precursors (NMN, NR), resveratrol, metformin (the planned TAME trial), rapamycin, senolytics: promising animal data, thin or absent human outcome data and real risks; taurine, omega-3 and vitamin D (DO-HEALTH trial); why supplements are loosely regulated; what has stronger evidence than any pill.

articles.title: Blue Zones: The Lessons and the Limits
articles.brief: What the Blue Zones idea claims, the shared habits (natural movement, mostly plant-based diets, purpose, social ties), the critique that some extreme-age data are unreliable (Saul Newman's work on record errors), what holds up regardless of the labels, how to apply the sound parts.

articles.title: Balance: The Fitness Skill That Keeps You Independent
articles.brief: Falls are the second leading cause of unintentional injury death worldwide (WHO: about 684,000 deaths a year), about 1 in 4 adults over 65 falls each year (CDC), the 10-second one-leg stand study (Araujo 2022), exercise programmes that cut falls (Sherrington Cochrane review: about 23%; tai chi; Otago), simple home balance drills by level, home hazards, medication review, vision.

articles.title: Alcohol and Your Health: What the Evidence Says Now
articles.brief: WHO 2023 statement that no level of consumption is risk-free, alcohol as a group 1 carcinogen (at least seven cancer types), why the old 'moderate drinking protects the heart' finding is doubted (sick-quitter bias, Mendelian randomisation), national guidelines (UK 14 units/week; Canada 2023 guidance; US Dietary Guidelines), what counts as a standard drink, benefits of cutting down, signs of dependence and where to get help.

articles.title: How to Quit Smoking (and Vaping): What Actually Works
articles.brief: WHO: tobacco kills more than 7 million people a year; timeline of benefits after quitting; methods ranked by evidence: combination nicotine replacement, varenicline, cytisine, bupropion, behavioural support; Cochrane review on nicotine e-cigarettes for quitting and the unknowns about long-term vaping; managing cravings and relapse; quitting vaping.

articles.title: Sitting All Day? Here's What Actually Offsets It
articles.brief: Sedentary time and health risk, Ekelund 2016 Lancet (about 60-75 minutes a day of moderate activity eliminated the excess mortality risk of long sitting) and Ekelund 2020 BMJ, breaking up sitting (short walking breaks improved glucose and blood pressure; Duran 2023), standing desks evidence (reduce sitting, modest health effect), desk setup basics, movement snacks.

articles.title: How to Build Habits That Actually Stick
articles.brief: How habits form (cue, routine, reward; context-dependent repetition), Lally 2010 (median 66 days, range 18-254), implementation intentions (Gollwitzer), habit stacking, making it easy by reducing friction, tracking, self-compassion after lapses, identity framing, breaking bad habits by changing cues, pitfalls of relying on motivation.

articles.title: Screen Time and Your Health: A Calm, Evidence-Based Take
articles.brief: What the research does and does not show (small average associations with wellbeing; content and displacement matter more than hours), sleep effects, digital eye strain and the 20-20-20 habit, blue-light glasses lack evidence (Cochrane 2023), posture and neck, children and teens guidance (WHO for under-5s), practical boundaries such as notifications, phone-free bedroom and greyscale.

articles.title: Sunlight, Nature and Health: Go Outside, It's Evidence-Based
articles.brief: White 2019 Scientific Reports (120 minutes a week in nature linked with better health and wellbeing), green space and mental health, daylight for the body clock and mood, myopia in children (outdoor time is protective), vitamin D and sun safety balance, forest-bathing studies and their limits, ways to get outdoors in cities.

articles.title: Caffeine: The Benefits, the Limits and the Fine Print
articles.brief: How caffeine works, typical amounts in coffee, tea, energy drinks and cola, up to 400 mg/day for most adults and 200 mg in pregnancy (FDA, EFSA), coffee and health outcomes (umbrella reviews link 3-4 cups a day with lower mortality; association only), performance effects (3-6 mg/kg; ISSN), anxiety, sleep and reflux, dependence and withdrawal, energy drinks and young people, pure caffeine powder danger.

articles.title: Saunas, Cold Plunges and Heat: Health Tool or Hype?
articles.brief: Finnish cohort data on sauna and cardiovascular outcomes (Laukkanen 2015; observational), plausible mechanisms, cold-water immersion evidence (modest and mixed; blunts muscle-growth signalling when used right after strength training), risks (cold shock, arrhythmia, drowning, alcohol with sauna), who should avoid them, heat illness basics, sensible protocols.

articles.title: How Your Immune System Works: A Guided Tour
articles.brief: Barriers, innate immunity, adaptive immunity (B cells, T cells, antibodies, memory), inflammation and fever as tools, how vaccines use memory, when the system misfires (allergy, autoimmunity) or is weakened, what affects immune function across life, the gut and immunity.

articles.title: Cold, Flu or COVID? How to Tell and What to Do
articles.brief: Symptom patterns and onset, why testing is the only sure way, home care (rest, fluids, paracetamol or ibuprofen as labelled, honey for cough in adults and children over 1), who should seek antivirals early (high-risk groups), staying home and when you are less contagious, red flags for urgent care, prevention.

articles.title: Vaccines for Adults: The Ones People Forget
articles.brief: Why adults need vaccines, commonly recommended ones (annual flu; COVID-19 per current national advice; tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis boosters; shingles from around 50; pneumococcal; HPV; hepatitis B; RSV for older adults and in pregnancy; MMR if not immune), travel vaccines, pregnancy, how safety is monitored, common side effects, check your own national schedule because recommendations differ and change.

articles.title: Antibiotics: When They Help and When They Hurt
articles.brief: Antibiotics treat bacteria, not viruses such as colds and flu; antimicrobial resistance burden (Lancet 2022: about 1.27 million deaths directly attributable in 2019); common illnesses that usually do not need antibiotics; side effects including C. difficile; how to take them (as prescribed, never leftovers or sharing); why 'finish the course' advice is being refined; what individuals can do.

articles.title: Can You Really Boost Your Immune System?
articles.brief: Why 'boosting' is the wrong frame (balance, not maximum), what supports normal function: sleep (Prather 2015: short sleepers were over four times more likely to catch a cold), activity, nutrition, vaccines, not smoking, stress management; supplements: vitamin C (does not prevent colds for most; modestly shortens them), zinc (possibly shorter colds, low-certainty evidence), vitamin D (small effect in deficiency), echinacea and elderberry (weak evidence).

articles.title: Seasonal Allergies: A Relief Plan That Works
articles.brief: What hay fever is, common triggers, allergy vs cold, treatments ranked (steroid nasal sprays most effective for nasal symptoms; non-sedating antihistamines; eye drops; saline rinses made with boiled or distilled water), correct nasal spray technique, pollen avoidance, immunotherapy, link with asthma, why sedating antihistamines are discouraged.

articles.title: Fever: What It Means and When to Worry
articles.brief: What counts as fever (generally 38 C / 100.4 F or higher), why the body raises its temperature, how to measure by age, comfort-based home care, medicines used as labelled (no aspirin for children and teenagers), red flags: infants under 3 months with fever need urgent assessment, stiff neck, rash that does not fade, confusion, breathing difficulty, fever after travel or lasting more than about 3 days; febrile seizures.

articles.title: Headaches and Migraine: Types, Triggers and Treatment
articles.brief: Tension-type headache vs migraine vs cluster headache, the phases of a migraine and aura, triggers and why they are less certain than believed, acute treatment (simple analgesics and NSAIDs, triptans, gepants), preventive options including CGRP-targeting drugs, medication-overuse headache, lifestyle foundations, red flags (thunderclap onset, new neurological signs, fever with stiff neck, new headache after 50).

articles.title: Memory and Focus: What Actually Sharpens Your Brain
articles.brief: How memory works in brief, normal forgetting, what improves focus and memory with evidence: sleep, aerobic exercise, managing attention and the cost of task switching, spaced repetition and retrieval practice, treating hearing loss and depression; what does not: most nootropics and commercial brain-training games (FTC action against Lumosity in 2016); when memory problems need assessment.

articles.title: Concussion: Signs, Recovery and When to Return
articles.brief: What concussion is (loss of consciousness is not required), symptoms, emergency red flags, the first 24-48 hours of relative rest then gradual return (Amsterdam 2022 consensus statement), graduated return to learn and return to sport, persistent symptoms, second-impact concerns, children, repetitive head impacts and CTE in brief.

articles.title: Dementia or Normal Aging? The Early Signs to Know
articles.brief: Normal age-related changes vs warning signs, dementia as an umbrella term with types (Alzheimer's, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal), WHO: about 57 million people living with dementia, mild cognitive impairment, reversible mimics (B12 deficiency, thyroid disease, depression, medicines, sleep apnea), how diagnosis works including blood biomarkers, anti-amyloid drugs (lecanemab, donanemab) with modest benefit and risks, supporting someone.

articles.title: ADHD in Adults: Signs, Diagnosis and What Helps
articles.brief: What ADHD is, how it presents in adults and especially women, prevalence (about 2.5% persistent adult ADHD; Song 2021), how diagnosis works (childhood onset, impairment, ruling out mimics), treatment (stimulant and non-stimulant medication, CBT, coaching, environmental strategies), sleep and exercise, strengths, the limits of self-diagnosis from social media.

articles.title: Dizziness and Vertigo: What's Spinning and Why
articles.brief: Types of dizziness (vertigo, lightheadedness, imbalance), common causes: BPPV with repositioning manoeuvres such as the Epley, vestibular neuritis, vestibular migraine, Meniere's disease, postural hypotension, medicines; stroke red flags (sudden onset with double vision, slurred speech, weakness, severe headache or inability to walk); vestibular rehabilitation.

articles.title: Brain Food: What to Eat for a Sharper, Healthier Brain
articles.brief: Dietary patterns over single foods: Mediterranean and MIND diets (observational support; the 2023 NEJM MIND trial found no significant difference from a control diet over three years), omega-3 and fish, berries and flavonoids, leafy greens, B vitamins only in deficiency, alcohol, COSMOS multivitamin cognition findings, what supplements do not do.

articles.title: Low Back Pain: What Works (and What Doesn't)
articles.brief: How common it is (leading cause of disability worldwide; WHO: about 619 million people in 2020), most cases are non-specific and improve within weeks, stay active rather than resting in bed, exercise therapy, heat, NSAIDs short term, why routine imaging is discouraged, what has weak evidence, psychological approaches for persistent pain (WHO 2023 guideline), red flags including cauda equina syndrome.

articles.title: Osteoporosis and Bone Health: Building a Stronger Frame
articles.brief: Peak bone mass by about 30, bone loss after menopause, risk factors, DXA scans and T-scores (-2.5 or lower), FRAX, calcium (about 1,000-1,200 mg/day mainly from food) and vitamin D, resistance and impact exercise (LIFTMOR trial), falls prevention, medicines (bisphosphonates and others), men get it too.

articles.title: Arthritis: Osteoarthritis vs. Rheumatoid, Explained
articles.brief: How the two differ (mechanical vs autoimmune; morning stiffness under 30 minutes vs over an hour; joint pattern), osteoarthritis management (exercise as core treatment, weight loss, topical NSAIDs; glucosamine evidence is weak), rheumatoid arthritis needs early disease-modifying drugs to prevent damage, gout in brief, when to see a doctor quickly.

articles.title: Knee Pain: Common Causes and Exercises That Help
articles.brief: Pain location as a clue (front: patellofemoral pain; inside or outside: meniscus or ligament; diffuse in older adults: osteoarthritis), load management, strengthening hips and quadriceps, running does not appear to wear out healthy knees (Alentorn-Geli 2017), arthroscopy for degenerative knees is not recommended (BMJ 2017 guideline), injury red flags (locking, giving way, rapid swelling).

articles.title: Posture and 'Tech Neck': Myths, Facts and Fixes
articles.brief: No single perfect posture; evidence linking posture to pain is weak; staying in one position too long matters more; your best posture is your next posture; neck and upper-back strengthening and movement breaks; workstation basics; posture braces lack evidence; red flags such as arm weakness or numbness.

articles.title: Sprains and Strains: Modern First Aid (Beyond RICE)
articles.brief: Sprain vs strain, grades, evolution from RICE to PEACE and LOVE (Dubois and Esculier, BJSM 2020), the debate on ice and anti-inflammatories in the first days, early protected movement and loading, Ottawa ankle rules for when an X-ray is needed, typical rehabilitation timeline, preventing re-injury with balance and strength work.

articles.title: Running Injuries: How to Avoid the Usual Suspects
articles.brief: Most common injuries (runner's knee, shin splints, Achilles and patellar tendinopathy, plantar fasciitis, IT band syndrome, stress fractures), training-load errors as the main cause, the 10% rule is a guide rather than a law, strength training for runners, shoe choice by comfort, cadence, pain rules during return, stress-fracture warning signs and RED-S.

articles.title: Health Screenings by Age: Your Checklist
articles.brief: Decade-by-decade guide based mainly on USPSTF recommendations with notes on international variation: blood pressure, lipids, diabetes screening (35-70 with overweight or obesity), cervical (21-65), breast (40-74), colorectal (45-75), lung (50-80 with a 20 pack-year history), osteoporosis (women 65+), abdominal aortic aneurysm (men 65-75 who have smoked), hepatitis C, HIV, depression and anxiety, skin, eyes and dental; overdiagnosis and shared decisions.

articles.title: Understanding Your Blood Tests: A Plain-English Guide
articles.brief: Why reference ranges vary by lab and what they mean (the central 95% of healthy people), full blood count, basic metabolic panel and kidney function (creatinine, eGFR), liver enzymes, lipid panel, HbA1c and glucose, TSH, ferritin and iron studies, vitamin D and B12, CRP; what slightly abnormal results usually mean; fasting; questions to ask.

articles.title: First Aid Basics Everyone Should Know
articles.brief: Unresponsive and not breathing normally: call emergency services, hands-only CPR at 100-120 compressions a minute about 5-6 cm deep, use an AED; choking response per current AHA and Red Cross guidance; severe bleeding (firm direct pressure, tourniquet if trained); burns (cool running water, ideally 20 minutes); recovery position; seizures; anaphylaxis and adrenaline auto-injectors; suspected stroke and heart attack. Encourage a certified course; verify current guideline details.

articles.title: How to Get More Out of a Doctor's Appointment
articles.brief: Preparation (top concerns first, symptom timeline, medication and supplement list, family history), the Ask Me 3 questions, repeat-back, shared decision-making and BRAN (benefits, risks, alternatives, nothing), bringing someone along, accessing your records, second opinions, telehealth tips, speaking up when you feel dismissed.

articles.title: Know Your Numbers: 8 Health Metrics Worth Tracking
articles.brief: Blood pressure, LDL or non-HDL cholesterol, HbA1c or fasting glucose, waist-to-height ratio, resting heart rate, weekly activity minutes, sleep duration and a simple fitness marker; healthy ranges, how often to check, how to measure at home, and avoiding over-tracking. Link to the relevant /tools pages.

articles.title: The Home First-Aid Kit: What to Keep and Why
articles.brief: Essentials based on Red Cross style lists: dressings, bandages, tape, antiseptic, gloves, thermometer, tweezers, scissors, oral rehydration salts, pain and fever relief, antihistamine, any personal emergency medicines; storage and expiry checks, a travel version, emergency numbers and medical information, what not to keep (expired antibiotics, syrup of ipecac).

articles.title: Cancer Screening, Explained: Benefits, Limits and Choices
articles.brief: What screening is and why it suits only some cancers; lead-time bias and overdiagnosis; current evidence-based programmes (cervical, colorectal including stool tests vs colonoscopy, breast, lung for people with heavy smoking history, prostate as a shared decision); multi-cancer early detection blood tests are not yet proven to reduce deaths; symptoms always warrant assessment regardless of screening.

articles.title: Emergency, Urgent or Wait? How to Decide Where to Go
articles.brief: Symptoms that need emergency services now (chest pain, stroke signs, severe breathing difficulty, heavy bleeding, anaphylaxis, sudden severe headache, confusion, seizures, suicidal crisis, serious injury), problems suited to same-day or urgent care, what can wait for a routine appointment, telehealth and nurse advice lines, children and older adults, what to bring. Region-neutral wording.
